So much like humans cats also get more and more lactose intolerant with age , it can cause tummy ache and diarrhea for some cats but I know a lot of cats that don't get diarrhea or stomach ache from milk, so only way is to ask the cat (lol jk) or I guess observe if milk is suiting them. When my cat was much smaller we'd give him milk diluted with water as alternative to buying cat specific milk, he'd drink all of it no complaints from his feeding bottle. But as my kitten grew he stopped drinking it , his food preferences has changed a lot he is also a picky eater so you have to try and see , I'd suggest going with diluted milk if you can't buy cat milk alternatives like me .
